title: Onboarding — make Kadé safe and fast to set up before Monday's new starter
feature: Devin environment blueprints (initialize, maintenance, knowledge), the AGENTS.md hierarchy and its automatic-inclusion limit, Knowledge migrating to Skills, and choosing Ask Devin or an Agent session
prerequisites: Repo cloned, Node 22, `npm install` done at the root
Lab 00 warm-up done once (framing stems and the update skeleton)
Fixture path: nothing beyond the repository connection — the blueprint audit, the AGENTS.md budget tool and all three injectors run locally
Optional live path: permission to edit the repository blueprint in Settings → Environment and to start a snapshot build

matrix.fixture: Your clone plus `docs/blueprint.proposed.yaml`, the per-service `AGENTS.md` files, `.devin/` and `labs/01-onboarding/tools/agents-budget.mjs`.
matrix.note: Zero credentials and zero secret values. Every acceptance criterion can be met by reading and running the repo on a session VM.

matrix.integration: Devin environment settings (repo blueprint, snapshot builds) — optional
matrix.fixture: `docs/blueprint.proposed.yaml` is the reference blueprint; compare it with what Settings → Environment shows and run its `initialize` and `maintenance` commands by hand on a session VM.
matrix.note: Live: edit the repository blueprint and trigger a build. Needs settings access; the fixture path proves the same commands with exit codes.

matrix.fixture: `.devin/skills/kade-dev/SKILL.md` is the repo skill a Knowledge note becomes; the blueprint `knowledge:` section in `docs/blueprint.proposed.yaml` shows environment-level context.
matrix.note: Live: open Settings → Knowledge (or Skills) to see where migrated notes landed. Read-only is enough.

matrix.fixture: Answer your three questions from the repo yourself and record which mode you would have used and why.
matrix.note: Ask Devin needs the repository to be indexed in your organization; nothing here assumes it.

credentials.fixture_only_story: With the clone alone you audit every place setup knowledge lives today, run the blueprint commands by hand on a session VM to prove they work, measure the AGENTS.md hierarchy with the budget tool, and work through the three injectors on a throwaway branch. You do not save a blueprint in settings or trigger a snapshot build; you show the before and after text and the exit codes instead.
not_exercised: Saving the repository blueprint in Settings → Environment and watching a snapshot build (fixture path runs the same commands by hand)
Browsing migrated Knowledge in a live organization
Ask Devin over an indexed repository

scenarios.clean_state: The injector revert prints `reverted` and `git status --short` is clean (no `docs/SETUP.md`, no `services/api/src/AGENTS.md`, no `labs/01-onboarding/.env.lab`). `lab:reset` reseeds the local lab database from the seed spec. The budget tool lists six `AGENTS.md` files, all under the limit, with exit code 0. Without Docker, skip the second command: everything else in this lab needs only the clone.

injectors.name: contradictory-agents
injectors.behaviour: `bash labs/01-onboarding/injectors/inject.sh contradictory-agents` adds a deeper `services/api/src/AGENTS.md` whose test and reset instructions disagree with `services/api/AGENTS.md` and the root file. Decide which one Devin should follow, and make the contradiction disappear on a throwaway branch.

injectors.name: stale-setup-doc
injectors.behaviour: `bash labs/01-onboarding/injectors/inject.sh stale-setup-doc` restores the old new-starter page, `docs/SETUP.md`, the one Jonas still trusts. It names a service that no longer exists, an old runtime and a database reset line. Decide what happens to it.

injectors.name: missing-paygate-secret
injectors.behaviour: `bash labs/01-onboarding/injectors/inject.sh missing-paygate-secret` writes `labs/01-onboarding/.env.lab` in which the webhook signing key differs between the fake payment provider and the services. Explain what a new engineer would see, and where the key's name (never its value) should be documented.
